stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
In a three-year trial, agronomist Lucía Ferrer found that soybeans planted into fields that had held a winter cover crop of cereal rye yielded 18 percent more than soybeans in fields left bare over winter. Because rye's dense roots are known to penetrate compacted soil layers, Ferrer concluded that the yield gain resulted from rye loosening the soil.

Text 2
Ferrer's yield figures are not in doubt. But soil-moisture probes installed in a follow-up study showed that rye residue left on the surface kept summer soil markedly wetter, and in dry years moisture alone can raise soybean yields by that much. The gain may owe little to changes in soil structure.
choices: Soybeans planted after a winter rye cover crop yielded more than soybeans planted in fields left bare over winter.
The soybean yield gain in Ferrer's trial resulted mainly from rye roots breaking up compacted layers of soil.
Ferrer's trial likely overstated how much more soybeans yielded in rye fields than in fields left bare.
Rye residue raises soybean yields chiefly by keeping the soil wetter during summers with little rainfall.
explanation: Split Text 1 into its observation (soybeans after rye yielded 18 percent more) and its inference (rye roots loosened the soil). Text 2 says outright that Ferrer's yield figures are 'not in doubt' and argues only with the cause, pointing to soil moisture instead. The one thing both authors accept is the observation itself: soybeans after rye outyielded soybeans in bare fields.

B.why: You picked Text 1's inference. Text 2 says the gain 'may owe little to changes in soil structure,' so the author of Text 2 would not accept this claim.

C.why: You assumed Text 2 attacks Ferrer's data. It explicitly says her yield figures are 'not in doubt.' Text 2 accepts the observation and questions only the explanation.

D.why: You picked Text 2's rival explanation, and you made it firmer than Text 2's hedged 'may.' Ferrer credits loosened soil, not moisture, so she would not agree.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
Over six weeks, seismometers beneath the long-dormant Arvel volcano recorded a swarm of small earthquakes whose sources grew steadily shallower, from roughly 10 kilometers deep to 3. Since rock fractures as it is forced apart, the monitoring team concluded that magma was rising toward the surface.

Text 2
Although the swarm's upward migration is well documented, a denser seismometer array later revealed low-frequency tremors typical of fluids moving through cracks. Pressurized water and gas escaping a deep, stationary magma body could have fractured rock at ever shallower depths; it is difficult to exclude a scenario in which no magma rose at all.
choices: Magma beneath the Arvel volcano rose to within roughly 3 kilometers of the surface during the swarm.
The depths assigned to the earthquakes were likely inaccurate before the denser array was installed.
The earthquakes in the swarm beneath the Arvel volcano originated at progressively shallower depths.
Water and gas escaping a stationary magma body, rather than rising magma, produced the swarm.
explanation: Text 1's observation is earthquakes migrating upward, and its inference is rising magma. Text 2 opens by granting that the upward migration 'is well documented,' then proposes escaping fluids as another cause. Both authors therefore accept that the earthquakes came from progressively shallower depths.

A.why: You picked Text 1's conclusion. Text 2 raises the possibility that 'no magma rose at all,' so its author would not sign on to this.

B.why: You took Text 2 to be challenging the measurements. It calls the migration 'well documented' and attacks only the inference that magma caused it.

D.why: You turned Text 2's hedge ('could have,' 'difficult to exclude') into a firm claim, and Text 1's team attributes the swarm to rising magma. Neither author would agree with this as worded.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
In the year after Halford banned smoking in restaurants and bars, emergency room visits for asthma attacks in the city fell by 22 percent. Health officials attributed the decline to the ban, reasoning that it sharply reduced residents' exposure to secondhand smoke.

Text 2
The drop in visits was real, but the same year the region's last coal-fired power plant shut down. Neighborhood-level air monitors show that fine-particle pollution fell most steeply in precisely the districts where asthma visits declined most, and such a reduction could by itself have produced the city's improvement.
choices: Halford's restaurant smoking ban was the primary reason fewer residents sought emergency care for asthma.
Emergency room visits for asthma in Halford declined during the year after the smoking ban took effect.
Hospital records likely overcounted the decline in asthma-related emergency room visits in Halford.
The closing of the coal-fired plant, not the smoking ban, accounted for Halford's drop in asthma visits.
explanation: Text 1 moves from an observation (asthma visits fell 22 percent) to a cause (the smoking ban). Text 2 grants that 'the drop in visits was real' and offers the plant closure as another possible cause. The shared ground is the observation: asthma visits fell in the year after the ban.

A.why: You picked the officials' inference. Text 2 argues that the plant closure 'could by itself' explain the drop, so its author would not accept the ban as the primary reason.

C.why: You assumed Text 2 disputes the data. It states plainly that the drop 'was real' and argues only about what caused it.

D.why: You hardened Text 2's 'could' into a definite claim, and Text 1 credits the ban. Neither author would endorse this statement.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
In a twelve-year study of 9,000 adults, those who reported eating nuts at least five times a week developed heart disease at a 30 percent lower rate than those who rarely ate nuts. The researchers concluded that the unsaturated fats abundant in nuts protect the heart.

Text 2
Reanalyzing the same food diaries with a detailed dietary-pattern score, Okafor found that frequent nut eaters also consumed far less processed meat. Nuts may simply have displaced harmful foods; that substitution alone could yield the lower rate, whatever nuts' fat content.
choices: The unsaturated fats in nuts are responsible for the lower rate of heart disease among frequent nut eaters.
The study's participants likely overreported how often they ate nuts when keeping their food diaries.
Eating less processed meat explains most of the reduced heart disease rate seen in frequent nut eaters.
Participants who ate nuts frequently developed heart disease at a lower rate than those who rarely did.
explanation: Text 1's observation is the 30 percent lower rate among frequent nut eaters, and its inference is that nut fats protect the heart. Text 2 reuses 'the same food diaries,' which means it accepts the data, and proposes substitution as another cause. Both authors would agree that frequent nut eaters had a lower rate of heart disease.

A.why: You picked Text 1's inference. Text 2 says the lower rate could arise 'whatever nuts' fat content,' so its author would not accept this.

B.why: You assumed Text 2 rejects the diary data. Okafor builds the reanalysis on those same diaries and challenges only the conclusion drawn from them.

C.why: You picked Text 2's rival explanation and made it more certain than its 'may simply' and 'could.' The authors of Text 1 credit nut fats, so they would disagree.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
Between the 2021 and 2023 seasons, the average 100-meter time among elite sprinters fell by 0.12 seconds, a large margin in an event decided by hundredths. Over the same period, most sprinters adopted spikes with stiff carbon-fiber plates, and biomechanist Ines Valk concluded that the plates' return of stored energy produced the faster times.

Text 2
Valk's times are accurate. Yet when the race results are sorted by venue, the improvement is concentrated at stadiums that installed new, more resilient track surfaces during those years. A springier track could produce the same gains whatever spikes athletes wore.
choices: Carbon-fiber plates in sprinters' spikes were the main source of the faster 100-meter times after 2021.
Elite sprinters' average 100-meter times were faster in the 2023 season than in the 2021 season.
The timing systems at major stadiums exaggerated the improvement in sprinters' 100-meter times.
Carbon-plated spikes return more energy to sprinters when they are used on more resilient tracks.
explanation: Text 1 observes faster average times and infers that carbon plates caused them. Text 2 begins 'Valk's times are accurate,' then names a different cause, the new track surfaces. Both authors accept that average times improved from 2021 to 2023.

A.why: You picked Valk's inference. Text 2 argues the tracks could produce the gains 'whatever spikes athletes wore,' so its author would not grant the plates top billing.

C.why: You took Text 2 to be disputing the measurements. It opens by calling Valk's times accurate and objects only to her explanation.

D.why: You were drawn by technical terms from both texts. Neither author says that plates and tracks work together. Text 2 presents the track as an alternative to the plates.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
At the Neolithic settlement of Drevna, excavators uncovered a layer of charcoal, scorched clay walls, and charred grain spanning every house, radiocarbon-dated to about 5200 BCE—the moment the village was abandoned. The team concluded that raiders had set the village ablaze, driving out its inhabitants.

Text 2
Drevna's burn layer and its date are not in question. However, at many Neolithic sites in the region, residents deliberately burned their own homes when leaving them, apparently as a closing ritual. Drevna has yielded no weapons and no skeletons showing injury, so the fire could just as easily mark such a ceremony.
choices: Drevna's inhabitants abandoned the village after attackers deliberately set fire to all of its houses.
The radiocarbon dates from Drevna's charcoal are likely too imprecise to tie the fire to its abandonment.
Drevna's residents burned their own houses as a closing ritual when they left the settlement.
A fire that left charred remains across Drevna's houses dates to about when the village was abandoned.
explanation: Text 1 observes a burn layer dated to the abandonment and infers a raid. Text 2 says the burn layer 'and its date are not in question' and offers ritual burning as another cause. Both authors therefore accept that a fire across the houses dates to about the time of abandonment.

A.why: You picked Text 1's conclusion. Text 2 notes there are no weapons or injured skeletons and offers a peaceful explanation, so its author would not agree.

B.why: You assumed Text 2 attacks the dating. It explicitly accepts both the burn layer and its date, and argues only about who set the fire and why.

C.why: You stated Text 2's alternative as fact, though Text 2 says only that the fire 'could just as easily' mark a ritual. Text 1 attributes it to raiders, so neither author holds this view as worded.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
Repeated dive surveys of the Selan reef showed that between 2012 and 2022 the number of parrotfish fell by 40 percent while the area covered by fleshy macroalgae doubled. Because parrotfish graze algae off coral, the survey team concluded that the loss of these grazers had allowed algae to overrun the reef.

Text 2
While the survey's counts match my own, water samples from the same sites reveal that nitrogen levels tripled over that decade as coastal farms expanded upstream. Nutrient enrichment can drive algal growth faster than any grazer could check, so the algae might have spread even with parrotfish numbers unchanged.
choices: During the decade when parrotfish numbers on the Selan reef declined, macroalgae cover on the reef increased.
The dive surveys probably undercounted the parrotfish that were living on the Selan reef during the decade.
Nitrogen runoff from coastal farms, rather than lost grazing, caused macroalgae to spread across the reef.
The decline in parrotfish grazing is what allowed fleshy macroalgae to overrun the Selan reef's coral.
explanation: Text 1 pairs two observations, fewer parrotfish and more algae, and infers that the first caused the second. Text 2 concedes that 'the survey's counts match my own,' then proposes nitrogen enrichment as another driver. Both authors accept that algae cover grew while parrotfish declined.

B.why: You assumed Text 2 rejects the survey. Its author says the counts match their own and questions only the causal link.

C.why: You turned Text 2's 'might have spread' into a definite cause, and the survey team in Text 1 blames lost grazing. Neither author would agree with this as worded.

D.why: You picked Text 1's inference. Text 2 argues the algae could have spread 'even with parrotfish numbers unchanged,' so its author would not accept it.

stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
stimulus:
Text 1
Space telescope data show that the star HD 70221 dims at irregular intervals, sometimes losing up to 20 percent of its light for days at a time. Since no planet could block that much light so unevenly, astronomers proposed that a swarm of disintegrating comets circling the star is passing in front of it.

Text 2
The dimming events are not disputed. Infrared observations, however, detect none of the extra glow that dust warmed by the star should emit. The light could instead be blocked by a clumpy cloud of cold interstellar dust drifting between the star and Earth, far from the star itself.
choices: A swarm of disintegrating comets orbiting HD 70221 is the source of the star's irregular dimming.
The absence of extra infrared glow shows that dust plays no part in the dimming of HD 70221.
HD 70221 has repeatedly lost a substantial share of its observed light at irregular intervals.
The irregular dimming of HD 70221 is likely an artifact of the space telescope's instruments.
explanation: Text 1 observes irregular dimming of up to 20 percent and infers orbiting comets. Text 2 says 'the dimming events are not disputed' and offers interstellar dust as another possible cause. Both authors agree that the star repeatedly loses a large share of its light at irregular intervals.

A.why: You picked Text 1's inference. Text 2 cites the missing infrared glow as a reason to doubt material warmed by the star, so its author would not accept the comet explanation.

B.why: You latched onto Text 2's technical detail and misread its logic. Text 2 uses the missing glow to move the dust away from the star, not to rule dust out. Its own explanation is cold interstellar dust.

D.why: You assumed Text 2 rejects the observation. It states that the dimming events are not disputed and challenges only what is causing them.
